subject: Technical deep-dive: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Technical deep-dive: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Hi Patricia —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the items we agreed to validate. Please ping if I missed anything.

High-level goals you shared:
- Serve interactive product-recommendation chat inside Acme's web app with 95th percentile latency target of <= 120 ms for conversational requests.
- Sustained throughput of ~250 requests/min during peak shopping hours (spiky bursts up to ~800 rpm).
- Data residency in US; all PII must be encrypted at rest and keys managed via Acme KMS.

Primary pain points:
- Current hosted vendor has unpredictable tail latency under burst loads.
- High per-token cost due to lack of batching and cache reuse.
- Need for a private deployment option behind Acme VPC for compliance.

Technical ask list (what we committed to follow up on):
1) Confirm model choices and quantization impact on latency/cost for your workload.
2) Provide a deployment topology (private VPC + dedicated GPU pools) that meets the SLOs and a fallback routing plan for outages.
3) Detail autoscaling behavior for bursty traffic and caching strategy to keep costs down.
4) Share a short SLA and cost estimate for an initial pilot (3 months).

What we covered on the call (summary):
- We suggested 2 topology options: Dedicated on-hosted Redwood Dedicated (single-tenant GPU pool) vs Private deployment in your AWS VPC using our Private control plane.
- Discussed model variants: Llama-2-70B-quant and an 8-bit quantized 34B variant for lower-latency inference.
- Explained KV/prefix caching to reduce repeated context recomputation for conversational sessions.

Attachments: redwood-slo-proposal.pdf, deployment-diagram.png

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa: deliver a short SLO + topology proposal and pilot cost estimate (due Wed 3/4).
- Dev: outline recommended instance types, batching params, and expected tokens/sec for each model variant (technical note attached).
- Patricia / Samir: confirm compliance constraints (KMS ARN, expected retention windows) and available pilot dates.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this running for you.

—
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches our internal notes. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 120 ms target is end-to-end (app front-end to response render). We typically add ~30 ms for network and client processing, so target for inference should be <= 90 ms 95th pctl.
- We will need to use our KMS (arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:987654321:key/abcd-1234) for model encryption and data at rest.
- For compliance we need 13-month retention for request logs and ability to produce audit logs on request.

Questions:
1) Is the 34B quantized variant realistically able to hit <= 90 ms p95 for short conversational prompts (~40 tokens) with batching disabled for lowest latency?
2) In private deployment, can you support bringing-your-own-KMS and route logs to our S3 without them leaving the VPC?

We can tentatively run a pilot starting week of 3/23 for 4 weeks. Samir will own scheduling of the infra touches.

-Patricia
VP Product — Acme Corp
patricia.gomez@acmecorp.com | +1 212-555-0199
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Patricia / team —

Quick technical response to the two specific questions and rough numbers you can use for planning. Happy to do a short screenshare if helpful.

Q1 — 34B quantized variant (8-bit) latency:
- For short prompts (~40 tokens) with batching disabled and GPU-local KV cache warm, we expect p50 ~25-35 ms, p95 ~70-95 ms on an NVIDIA A10G / H100s-class instance depending on sequence length and model architecture. The 90 ms p95 target is achievable in many configs; margin depends on quantization and kernel vendor (we include optimized kernels in our runtime).
- If you need tighter tail-latency guarantees, options: smaller model (e.g., 13B quantized), aggressive prefix caching, or provisioned single-request instances (more expensive).

Q2 — Private deployment + BYO KMS + logs:
- Yes — our Private offering supports customer-managed KMS keys and Sink connectors to write logs to your S3 buckets inside the VPC. We deploy control plane components outside your VPC and inference plane inside; audit logs can be exported via an encrypted SSE-KMS S3 bucket.
- We support VPC Endpoints and strict egress controls; no data needs to traverse public internet for inference traffic.

Throughput / scaling notes (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline per-instance throughput (34B-8bit on A10G): ~80-120 requests/sec with small prompts and concurrent batching enabled. With batching disabled for strict latency targets, per-instance RPS drops to ~10-25 depending on concurrency.
- To hit sustained 250 requests/min (~4.2 RPS) the requirement is modest; to handle 800 rpm burst (~13.3 RPS) and maintain <120 ms p95 we recommend a small pool of 4-6 GPU workers with autoscaling and burst headroom.

Recommended pilot topology (attachment: deployment-diagram.png):
- Private inference plane in Acme VPC: 4 x A10G instances in a dedicated ASG behind a regional load balancer.
- Control plane: Redwood-managed with private peering to the VPC for orchestration.
- KV cache: per-worker in-memory cache with optional Redis-based shared cache for session reuse.
- Fallbacks: if private pool exhausted, route to Redwood Dedicated (isolated tenant) in same region.

We will attach a short technical note with expected tokens/sec and cost estimates per model variant (see redwood-slo-proposal.pdf).
